content: A man who has not passed through the inferno of his passions has never overcome them.
author: Carl Jung
sourceWork: Modern Man in Search of a Soul (1933)
story:
This insight touches directly on the messy reality of human nature. Living in pretense takes an enormous amount of mental energy. When you constantly manage impressions to please others, you end up feeling like an imposter in your own skin.

In Carl Jung's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. Honesty with yourself can feel uncomfortable at first, but it is the only ground upon which a real life can be built. When you stop lying to yourself about your feelings, your energy is immediately freed up.
reflectionPrompt: When you look back on past hardships, how did navigating them expand your capacity for strength?
